title: Denormalized listing search documents in MongoDB
name: Listing search indexer

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps the denormalized seller data in search documents up to date? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: onSellerProfileChanged uses updateOne with the filter {"seller.id": sellerId}. A seller typically has many listings, but updateOne modifies only the first matching document. All other listings keep the old displayName and rating in search results until each is individually re-indexed. It should be updateMany.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does each search document embed the seller's displayName and rating instead of just the seller id?
choices: MongoDB cannot store ObjectId references inside subdocuments
So search results can be returned from one collection without a per-result lookup into sellers, at the cost of propagating seller changes
Embedding makes the keywords index smaller
It lets search() filter by seller rating using the keywords index
choiceQuestions.explanation: Embedding read-time data is the classic denormalization tradeoff: search() projects seller.displayName and seller.rating directly, avoiding N extra lookups, but changes to a seller must be fanned out. ObjectId references are fine in subdocuments, embedding doesn't affect the keywords index size, and search() doesn't filter on rating.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A query searches for "red bike" in category "sports" under $500. Which statement about matching is correct?
choices: Only listings whose title is exactly 'red bike' match
Matching is case-sensitive, so 'Red Bike' titles are excluded
Listings whose keywords contain both 'red' and 'bike' match, regardless of order or case
choiceQuestions.explanation: tokenize lowercases and splits both titles and queries, and the filter uses keywords: {$all: terms}, requiring every term. $all is not OR, there's no exact-title match, and lowercasing on both sides removes case sensitivity.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The same listing.upserted event is delivered twice. What is the result?
choices: One search document, because replaceOne with upsert on _id overwrites the same document
Two search documents for the listing
The second delivery throws a duplicate key error
The second delivery is skipped because indexedAt is already set
choiceQuestions.explanation: indexListing uses replaceOne({_id}, doc, {upsert: true}), which is idempotent per _id: the second call replaces the document with the same content. No duplicate is created, upsert on _id doesn't raise duplicate key errors here, and indexedAt is never checked.
